snippet.title: Nat King Cole Staying Was the Protest
snippet.description:
🏠 In 1948, Nat King Cole bought a Tudor mansion in Hancock Park, an all-white Los Angeles neighborhood. His neighbors formed a property owners association, threatened lawsuits, tried to buy the house back, and then the harassment began: a racial slur burned into his lawn and a poisoned family dog.

🎤 When the neighbors’ lawyer said they didn’t want “undesirable” people in the neighborhood, Cole replied that if he saw any, he’d be the first to complain. He never left. He and his wife Maria raised their children there, including Natalie Cole, and the family kept the house until 1972.

📺 In 1956, white men attacked him on stage in Birmingham, Alabama, and he became the first major Black musician to host a national TV variety show, which no national sponsor would back. He said he was an entertainer, not an activist. But in Hancock Park, simply staying was the protest.

👇 Is quietly refusing to leave real activism, or did a star that big owe more? Comment STAYED or SPOKE UP and defend your answer. Type UNFORGETTABLE if his voice raised you. Like, share, and follow Black History Unfiltered for the Black history they didn’t teach us.

USC Annenberg Charlotta Bass Journalism and Justice Lab (Cynthia Kinyera), April 9, 2026, “The Hurdle at Hancock Park” - Shelley v. Kraemer timing, the neighbors’ association, the buyback attempt, the 1951 tax seizure
The Saturday Evening Post, July 17, 1954 (Richard G. Hubler), “$12,000-a-Week Preacher’s Boy” - the lawyer exchange, “GET OUT” signs, 100+ threatened lawsuits, rocks, the shot through the window, “I guess I’m a symbol to a lot of people”

Le projet LEO est une méga-constellation de satellites en orbite basse qui offrira un accès internet haut débit. Elle sera gérée par Kuiper Systems LLC, filiale d'Amazon. Cette constellation devrait être composée de 3 236 satellites. Les satellites devraient être placés sur 98 plans orbitaux répartis en trois couches orbitales : 590 km, 610 km et 630 km d'altitude.

Vulcan VC6L : La configuration de Vulcan est identifiable grâce à sa clé. Ce lancement s'effectue sur un VC4S . Le « V » signifie Vulcain, le « C » signifie Centaure, le « 6 » représente le nombre de propulseurs à poudre (jusqu'à six) et le « L » est la longueur du carénage de la charge utile, disponible en standard et long.
* Hauteur: 65.5m 
* Diamètre: 5.4 m
* Masse au décollage: 903 tonnes
* Étage: 2
Propulsion premier étage : 2 x BE-4 (Méthane liquide / Oxygène liquide)
Propulsion deuxième étage (Centaure) : 2 x RL-10C-X (Hydrogène liquide / Oxygène liquide) (Ce sont les mêmes moteurs d’étage supérieur utilisés par Atlas V / + de 400 vols réussis. Un nouvel étage Centaur raccourci spécialement conçu pour Amazon. Environ 1,8 m de moins que le Centaur V standard. Un tiers d'ergols en moins. Une masse structurelle réduite pour emporter davantage de satellites. Cette architecture est adaptée à des injections en orbite basse plutôt qu'aux missions nécessitant davantage d'énergie, notamment vers l'orbite géostationnaire.

snippet.title: The Lazy Soup I Make Every Sunday at 72 — One Pot, Five Suppers, Nothing to Chop
snippet.description:
#LazySoup #CookingForOne #SoupForOne
The lazy soup Nora makes every Sunday at 72 — one pot, five suppers, nothing to chop. Half an hour after church: rotisserie chicken, coleslaw mix, frozen onion and soup veg, white beans, and tomatoes in Walt's mother's blue enamel stockpot. Five jars. Five different "hats," Monday through Friday.

After Walt died she stopped cooking. Friend Bev (retired nurse) said the women who stop cooking are the ones she used to see in the hospital. Nora went back to Mama's wash-day soup: cook once on Sunday, heat and change the hat all week. Same soup, different hat — Marge's line. Shopping ~$15–18, nothing needs a knife. Coleslaw melts into the broth; rotisserie chicken is the other secret; lemon at the end like Grandma's last verse.

Full printable list below — tape it inside a cupboard door.

🖨️ PRINTABLE: THE SUNDAY POT + FIVE HATS
(About $15–18. No knife. Low-sodium broth; rinse beans; taste before salting.)

SUNDAY POT
- 1 rotisserie chicken (pull with 2 forks; bones frozen for broth)
- 1 carton (32 oz) low-sodium chicken broth
- Handful frozen chopped onion · ½ bag frozen soup veg · ½ bag coleslaw mix
- 2 cans white beans, rinsed · 1 can diced tomatoes
- Bay leaf, pinch thyme, black pepper · squeeze of lemon at the end
Simmer bones + broth ~20 min; remove bones. Add everything but chicken; simmer ~15 min until cabbage soft. Add chicken to warm. Ladle into 5 jars: 3 fridge (Mon–Wed), 2 freezer (Thu–Fri). Move freezer jars down the night before. Wash the pot once.

FIVE HATS
☐ Mon: plain bowl + buttered crackers (the honest first bowl)
☐ Tue: handful wide egg noodles ~8 min (or Mama's drop dumplings — don't peek)
☐ Wed: 2 spoonfuls salsa + cumin + canned green chiles; chips, cheese, lime
☐ Thu: Walt's cold soup — jarred grated ginger, lemon, lots of pepper; beaten egg into boiling soup
☐ Fri: 1–2 spoonfuls instant potato flakes; pour over a split biscuit

OTHER SUNDAY POTS (same 5-supper plan)
- Joyce: roasted red pepper & white bean (jarred peppers, beans, broth, garlic powder; blend)
- Peggy: four-can chili (4 bean cans, tomatoes, chili seasoning, frozen onion)
- Shirley's: potato, bacon & cabbage (frozen diced potatoes, bacon pieces, coleslaw, broth)

⏱️ CHAPTERS

02:59 The nothing-to-chop shopping list

🍲 FOOD SAFETY NOTES

Refrigerate within 2 hours in shallow containers. Use fridge soup in 3–4 days; freeze the rest; thaw in the fridge, not on the counter. Reheat steaming hot throughout, 165°F (74°C). Boil before stirring in a raw egg. Rotisserie leftover meat: fridge within 2 hours; use in 3–4 days. Freezer-safe jars: ~1 inch headspace; don't move a jar from freezer into boiling water or a hot oven. Sodium runs high in rotisserie chicken, broth, beans, and salsa — low-sodium broth, rinse beans, taste before salting. Ginger in food amounts is usually fine; ask a pharmacist before large amounts if you take a blood thinner. Soft noodles/veg if chewing is hard.

snippet.description:

कभी-कभी हमें अपनी जिंदगी में जो परेशानियां दिखती हैं, वही किसी दूसरे के लिए एक ख्वाहिश होती हैं। इसलिए दूसरों की जिंदगी से अपनी जिंदगी की तुलना करने के बजाय, जो हमारे पास है उसकी कद्र करना सीखिए।

सीख: दूसरे की थाली में घी हमेशा ज्यादा दिखता है, लेकिन सुकून उसी को मिलता है जो अपनी जिंदगी को खुशी से जीना सीख लेता है। ❤️

वीडियो पसंद आए तो लाइक, शेयर और कमेंट जरूर करें। #emotionalstory #motivation #believeinkarma 

एक जरूरी सूचना: यह वीडियो AI (Artificial Intelligence) की मदद से बनाया गया है, लेकिन इसकी कहानी, स्क्रिप्ट, विचार और क्रिएटिव निर्देशन पूरी तरह मेरे द्वारा तैयार किए गए हैं।
